title: Eyes on the road: A bicycle simulator study of cyclists' gaze behavior while sharing the road with autonomous vehicles across infrastructure types
venue: Transportation Research Part F 121, 103711 (running header prints 'Psychology and Behaviour' without 'Traffic')
study_type: Laboratory bicycle-simulator experiment, within-subjects (11 scenarios); secondary analysis of gaze data from the experiment reported in Hammami & Borsos (2026)
vehicles: Conventional bicycle on simulator (model not reported); simulated AVs (constant 50 km/h, 1.5 m passing, roof LiDAR cue) and human-driven cars; no e-scooter
environment: Simulator: multi-screen display, lateral moving plate, speed-dependent fans; virtual 200 m straight segment of Szövetség Street, Győr (HU); shared road with sharrows (A) vs bike lane separated by continuous painted line, black (B,C) or red (D,E), 1.25 m or 1.5 m wide; 50 km/h; moderate traffic
sensors: Pupil Labs Neon wearable eye tracker (scene camera, gaze, pupil); simulator logging not reported
kinematic_sensors: not reported (no cyclist kinematics analysed)
cv_methods: Image-space aggregated gaze heatmaps (8-bit layers summed without normalisation); threshold-based attention area (>128) and mean intensity
fixation_definition: not reported (only conceptual definitions in Table 3; algorithm/thresholds not given)
gaze_metrics: Mean fixation duration, fixation rate (Hz), blink rate (/min), average blink duration, average saccade amplitude, PERCLOS; heatmap attention area (px) and mean intensity; pupil ΔP (baseline = median of first 5 s), ΔP IQR, left–right difference, valid-sample ratio
kinematic_metrics: not reported
statistics: Normality checks (test not named); per TPR level Friedman test across infrastructure, Holm-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank post hoc; Kendall's W and rank-biserial r; percentile bootstrap 95% CIs on reconstructed recording-level summaries; grouped Wilcoxon contrasts at 3 aggregation levels; heatmaps and pupil descriptive only; no mixed models
key_results: Saccade amplitude larger in separated lanes than shared at 0% TPR (χ²=14.56, p<.001, W=0.1456; A0–B0 pHolm=0.002 r=0.481; A0–D0 pHolm=0.010 r=0.399); grouped A vs BC pHolm=0.004, A vs DE pHolm=0.036; fixation duration infrastructure effect at 50% (χ²=7.96, p=.019) and 100% TPR (χ²=9.79, p=.044) but not 0%; no clear TPR effect; heatmap attention area largest B100 (71155.38 px), smallest A50 (58464.60 px); pupil ΔP −0.026 to +0.030 mm, overlapping
effect_sizes: Kendall's W 0.0084–0.1456; rank-biserial r 0.376–0.481; bootstrap A vs BC saccade median diff −0.13° (95% CI −0.34°, −0.04°); W values verified from χ²/(N(k−1))
limitations: Authors: simulator realism, single 200 m straight segment without intersections, learning/fatigue over 11 scenarios, young male-skewed sample, imputation, ET sensitivity to calibration/event parameters, heatmaps exploratory, TPR confounded with vehicle behaviour, pupillometry exploratory. Ours: detector parameters/rates unreported; saccade-amplitude units inconsistent (Fig. 3 ≈100 vs −0.13°); very long fixations (~1 s); N=49 cells tested as N=50; 'physically separated' = painted line; many uncorrected-across-family test sets; opposite direction to Guo et al. 2023 TRF
code_available: not reported (analysis script mentioned, not shared)
data_available: On request ('Data will be made available on request')
replicability_for_us: Infrastructure contrast and nonparametric stats (a); fixation/saccade metrics (b) at Aria 30 Hz with re-tuned detectors, saccade amplitude weak; blink/PERCLOS (b)/(d); pupillometry (c)/(d) outdoors; heatmaps (a) technically but (d) scientifically; TPR manipulation (c)
rq_informed: RQ2 (shared vs separated infrastructure); RQ1 (gaze metric choice); PPG decision by analogy (physiological proxy only exploratory)
page_refs: Participants p. 4 (PDF p. 4) Sec. 3.1; apparatus/Neon pp. 4–5 Sec. 3.2; Table 2 p. 5; design p. 5–6 Sec. 3.3; metrics Table 3 p. 7; heatmaps pp. 6–7 Sec. 3.5; pupillometry p. 7 Sec. 3.6; stats p. 8 Sec. 4.1; results pp. 8–12 Secs. 4.1–4.4; Table 5 p. 10; limitations pp. 13–14 Sec. 5.3; data availability p. 15

title: Bicycle performance monitoring on a two-way protected cycle lane related to different separation elements
study_type: Field study, instrumented bicycle + mobile eye tracker, within-subject across infrastructure sections
vehicles: One instrumented city bike (Almabike); no e-scooter
environment: Florence, protected bi-directional cycle paths; sections: curbs 300 m, vegetation 200 m, New Jersey barriers 100 m, curbs+parking 300 m
sensors: Tobii Pro Glasses 3; Garmin Edge 130 Plus; Avisaro 6-DOF IMU on rear seat; ANT+ cadence/speed sensor
kinematic_sensors: GPS 1 Hz (Garmin); seat IMU 100 Hz; cadence/speed 1 Hz
sync_method: Tap on bicycle seat (later 'handlebar tap') as common spike marker
fixation_definition: Tobii I-VT, velocity <30°/s; fixation duration >60 ms
gaze_metrics: % fixation count and % fixation duration on AOIs Front+FoE, Road, Side; gaze sample >85%
kinematic_metrics: Section speed (stops removed); vertical acc. high-passed, 1-s RMS → ISO 2631-1 comfort classes A–F
statistics: Shapiro–Wilk, Levene; one-way ANOVA + Tukey; Pearson correlations; MLR with VIF
key_results: Speed S1 14.94±1.78, S2 15.58±1.50, S3 12.02±1.35, S4 12.94±1.19 km/h (F(4,95)=30.655); speed r=0.469 with front fixation duration, −0.449 ISO class, −0.359 declared safety; MLR R²=0.318
effect_sizes: Pearson r, R²; my η² speed ≈0.56
limitations: Authors: N=20, one route, standard bicycle. Assessment: speed text/table mismatch, df errors, repeated measures ignored, non-ISO-compliant vibration processing, correlation table errors
data_available: On reasonable request (sensitivity; UNIBO controlled storage)
replicability_for_us: High: GPS/VIO section speed, AOI coding, I-VT on 30 Hz gaze (a/b); head-IMU vibration instead of seat (b); seat IMU/cadence (c)
page_refs: Sensors p.4–5 (PDF 4–5) Sec.2.1; route p.5–6 Sec.2.2; results p.7–15 Sec.3; Table 2 p.8; Table 6 p.13

title: How do different micro-mobility vehicles affect longitudinal control? Results from a field experiment
study_type: Controlled field experiment (proving ground), within-subject
vehicles: E-scooter Ninebot ES2; Segway Ninebot S; bicycle Monark Karin 3-VXL ridden assisted (e-bike) and unassisted
n_participants: 34 (9 F, 25 M); Segway: 25 rode, 14 with usable kinematics
environment: Proving ground, Chalmers/Gothenburg; no other road users
sensors: Vehicle IMU PhidgetSpatial 3/3/3 1044_B + Raspberry Pi 3B logger; infrastructure LiDAR HOKUYO UXM-30LAH-EWA
kinematic_sensors: Vehicle-mounted IMU (longitudinal acc.) fused with track-side LiDAR centroid via RTS smoother; rates not reported
gaze_metrics: not applicable
kinematic_metrics: Mean acceleration (2.5→16 km/h) and deceleration (16→2.5 km/h; Segway 12) = slope of linear speed–time fit + R²; braking distance; stop-line overshoot; response time command→1 km/h drop
statistics: GLMM (fitglme), participant random effect; gender, vehicle, maneuver fixed; post-hoc coefTest; alpha 0.05 Bonferroni
key_results: Decel. bicycle vs e-scooter (m/s²): comfort −1.50±0.51 vs −1.28±0.42; harsh −3.00±1.29 vs −2.21±0.59; unexpected −3.60±1.28 vs −2.23±0.71 (F=39, p≪0.001). Acc.: comfort 0.45±0.11 vs 0.56±0.19; harsh 0.76±0.28 vs 0.70±0.25. E-scooter longer braking distance and response time (F=6.7); stop line crossed 61% e-scooter vs 14% bike
effect_sizes: Not reported; my unpaired d bike vs e-scooter decel.: 0.47 comfort, 0.80 harsh, 1.35 unexpected
limitations: Authors: data loss, controlled repetitive tasks, single e-scooter model with electric brake, young sample. Assessment: rates/filters unreported, truncated windows inflate 'constant decel.', table/caption mislabels, no effect sizes
replicability_for_us: High: VIO/GPS speed windows + linear decel. fits on natural stops (a); response time needs visual-stimulus redefinition (b); vehicle IMU+LiDAR (c)

authors: Guo, Tavakoli, Angulo, Robartes, Chen & Heydarian
title: Psycho-physiological measures on a bicycle simulator in immersive virtual environments: how protected/curbside bike lanes may improve perceived safety
study_type: Laboratory VR (HMD) bicycle-simulator experiment, within-subjects (3 designs), multimodal sensing
vehicles: Trek Verve bicycle on Wahoo Kickr trainer/Climb/Headwind; steering and braking via HTC Vive controllers; virtual cars (4 models, constant 25 mph); no e-scooter
environment: Immersive VR replica (Unity/SteamVR) of Water Street, Charlottesville VA: four blocks, three intersections (signal at #3), 4% downhill segment; designs: as-built sharrows, curbside bike lane 1.2 m, protected bike lane 1.2 m + 0.3 m buffer with flexible delineators every 1.8 m; low traffic (0.9 passing vehicles on average)
sensors: HTC Vive Pro Eye with integrated Tobii Pro eye tracker; Unity C# logging (bike, headset, controllers, vehicles); OBS video (2 room cameras + VR POV); 2 Android smartwatches (SWEAR app) for HR and hand acceleration
eye_tracker: Tobii Pro integrated in HTC Vive Pro Eye (110° FOV)
kinematic_sensors: Unity logs 30 Hz (speed, position, heading, headset/controller pose, brake trigger); smartwatch accelerometer 100 Hz (hand; not analysed)
sync_method: Device clocks synced to an online server before each session; video timing from Windows file metadata; per-stream resampling (30/120/1 Hz); no hardware trigger; accuracy not reported
cv_methods: OpenCV for gaze-on-video overlay (3D gaze projected to 2D POV); OpenPose listed for room-video pose extraction (no results reported)
detection_tracking: not used (virtual object positions from Unity logs)
fixation_definition: PyGaze-adapted dispersion (I-DT) algorithm, minimum duration 25 ms, maximum dispersion 100 px (≈8.5° by Eq. 3 geometry, our computation) on 2D POV video
gaze_metrics: Horizontal gaze variability (SD, px); percentage of road centre (PRC: fixation duration within 12° = 142.88 px of modal fixation bin); mean fixation duration (s); stationary gaze entropy (100×100 px bins, 1 s rolling windows); gaze transition entropy (first-order Markov on fixations); gaze heat map
kinematic_metrics: Mean speed (km/h); mean lateral position (distance to curb, m); head pose logged but not analysed
statistics: One linear mixed model per DV (lme4), participant random effect; fixed: scenario, age (<35/≥35), gender, cyclist type, VR experience, realism of speed and steering, age×scenario and gender×scenario; Fisher's LSD post hoc; α=0.05; no multiplicity correction; HR change points by Bayesian change point (Barry & Hartigan; R bcp), threshold not reported; HR artefact handling not reported
key_results: Perceived safety higher for protected (β=1.531, SE 0.212) and curbside (β=1.286, SE 0.212) vs sharrows; speed lower in protected lane (13.88 vs 15.09 km/h; β=−1.209, SE 0.383); lateral position n.s. (p=0.068); horizontal gaze variability lower (curbside β=−16.349, protected β=−12.645 px); PRC higher (4.083, 2.558 pp); fixation duration longer (0.015, 0.014 s); SGE lower only for curbside (−0.224 bits); GTE n.s.; mean HR n.s. across designs; HR change points fewer (curbside β=−0.393, protected −0.360; 1.07/0.56/0.59 per min) and clustered before intersections
effect_sizes: Only unstandardised β, SE, p reported; Wald 95% CIs computable (e.g., speed −1.209 [−1.96, −0.46] km/h; HGV curbside −16.349 [−24.75, −7.95] px; HR change points curbside −0.393 [−0.677, −0.109]); no standardised effects, R² or ICC
limitations: Authors: VR simulator not fully real; short trials (HR rises with effort/fatigue); learning effects; only light-separation protected lane; need real-world benchmark; low traffic; HR 1 Hz, raw PPG affected by motion artefacts; regular cyclists only. Ours: stress inferred from unvalidated change-point counts confounded by grade/speed/exertion; no HR artefact handling reported; mislabelled 'random effects' (likely intercepts) and copy error; non-standard fixation thresholds; no multiplicity correction; no order term; controller steering; eye-in-head metrics only; text–result inconsistencies
code_available: Partial: Tobii–Unity setup and eye-tracking preprocessing scripts at https://git.io/JK3hq (Guo, 2022); licence not stated; not verified
replicability_for_us: Speed, gaze SD, PRC, heat maps, LMM, perceived-safety surveys (a); fixation/entropy metrics, lateral position, HR from Aria PPG, BCP, head pose (b); HR or change points as 'stress' and LSD (d); wrist accelerometry, OpenPose room video, design manipulation (c)
rq_informed: PPG/HR decision (primary); RQ2 (sharrows vs bike lanes); RQ1 (gaze dispersion metrics, speed, lateral position); RQ3 (speed reduction with gaze concentration)

title: Understanding Cyclists' Visual Behavior Using Eye-Tracking Technology: A Systematic Review
study_type: systematic review (PRISMA 2020; ChatGPT-3.5/ChatPDF-assisted screening; no quality appraisal; no meta-analysis)
vehicles: bicycles (real, instrumented, simulator); cars in 8 driver-only studies; e-scooter only in Pashkevich et al. 2022 [15]
n_participants: 25 included studies (610 identified, 38 duplicates, 572 screened, 84 sought, 83 assessed, 25 included); real-env mean N 22 (13-50 stated), virtual mean 46 (5-130), comparative mean 21 (6-40)
environment: 11 real traffic, 11 simulator (incl. 7 driving simulators), 3 real-vs-virtual comparisons; 14 Europe, 9 North America, 2 Asia
sensors: eye trackers plus GPS action cameras, instrumented bike (IMU, GPS, power, cadence), LiDAR [11], GSR/EDA, HR, breathing, smartwatch hand acceleration, VR head direction [22]
eye_tracker: Pupil Pro, Pupil Invisible, Pupil Core, Pupil Labs VR/AR, Tobii Pro Glasses 2, ASL Mobile Eye-XG, SMI ETG v1/2, Dikablis ETG 3, HTC Vive Pro Eye, FOVE, FOVIO, Smart Eye Pro DX, FaceLAB 5.0
et_rate_hz: as printed in Table A2: 25-120 Hz (mostly 30 or 60 Hz); several values conflict with device specs in Ma2024review
kinematic_sensors: real env: only 3/11 studies (speed, power, cadence, position); sim: 7/11 (speed, BRT, TTC, steering, cadence)
cv_methods: Faster R-CNN + Kalman filter object identification/tracking (Epigram AS) in Aasvik & Fyhri 2022 [19]; 'dwell-time fixation detection algorithm' (called unsupervised ML) in [14,17]
semantic_segmentation: not used (the review calls Faster R-CNN 'segmentation')
detection_tracking: Faster R-CNN + Kalman filter, 'traffic object' classes, Pupil Invisible scene video [19]; no validation metrics reported
fixation_definition: Table 6: >200 ms (Stelling-Konczak [9], Kircher & Ahlstrom 2020 [16], Pashkevich [15]); 80-500 ms (Mantuano [17]); >100 ms (Girgis [12]); 100 ms in 7 simulator studies; 100 ms min in dwell-time algorithm [14,17]
gaze_metrics: glance/fixation number, duration, % per AOI, frequency by direction/target; mean point of gaze X/Y; entry time of first fixation [21]; SGE/GTE [22]; pupil diameter [22]; gaze angle [29]; % saccades/blinks [31]
kinematic_metrics: speed (video distance/time in [15]), power, cadence, position, braking reaction time, TTC, steering, hand-acceleration-derived speed/steering [22]
statistics: GLMM, ANOVA, Wilcoxon, Z-tests, logistic and negative-binomial regression, paired t-tests, LMM, chi-square, correlation, Bland-Altman
key_results: intersections impose the greatest visual workload; complexity/pedestrian density/trucks/poor surfaces raise workload; experience -> longer fixations; Pashkevich: significant mode differences, e-scooter speeds too high, 261 violations; simulator vs field gaze differs (Gay 2023)
effect_sizes: none reported
limitations: authors: small samples, generalizability, selection bias, little ML, foveal bias/gaze != attention, experimenter confounds, fatigue/carry-over; AI screening bias. Assessment: driver-only studies included against stated criterion; PRISMA arithmetic off by one; reference and Hz inconsistencies
data_available: not applicable (extraction tables in Appendix A)
replicability_for_us: AOI glance/fixation metrics and thresholds replicable at 30 Hz; detector+tracker AOI adaptable on 15 fps RGB; head direction via VIO; hand-based steering proxy adaptable; GSR/power/cadence/cortisol not available
rq_informed: RQ1 (Pashkevich precedent), RQ2, RQ3 (entry time of first fixation, BRT/TTC templates), RQ4 (carry-over), RQ5 (smartwatch hand acceleration precedent)

title: Assessment of cyclists' cognitive workload through eye tracker and EEG sensors: Sensitivity to individual and external factors in a real-world experiment
venue: Transportation Research Part F: Psychology and Behaviour 119, 103563 (special issue ICTCT 2024-TRF)
study_type: Exploratory real-world field pilot study, single ride per participant, multimodal (eye tracking + EEG + vehicle GNSS/INS + OSM + NASA-TLX)
vehicles: Instrumented conventional-looking bicycle (model and e-assist not reported); no e-scooter
environment: Real urban traffic, Gdansk (Poland), daylight and favourable weather; raised separated cycle tracks, shared ped-cycle areas, signalised/unsignalised crossings, bus stops, commercial accesses
sensors: Pupil Invisible eye tracker (Companion app v1.4.21 on bike-mounted phone); NeuroSky MindWave Mobile 2 EEG; WitMotion WTGAHRS2 GNSS/INS on bicycle
eye_tracker: Pupil Invisible (Pupil Labs), 2 IR eye cameras 200 Hz, scene 30 Hz 82 deg FOV, accuracy ~4.6 deg
et_rate_hz: 200 (eye cameras); analysed at 15 Hz scene-frame rate
kinematic_sensors: Bicycle-mounted WTGAHRS2 GNSS/INS 5 Hz: lat/lon, speed, yaw, 3-axis linear acc, 3-axis angular velocity
sync_method: Gaze timestamps as master; Unix ms timestamps + WGS-84 position; linear interpolation of EEG (1 Hz eSense) and GNSS/INS to gaze timestamps; zero-speed start/end removed; NASA-TLX mapped to GNSS points via QGIS segments
cv_methods: Custom tool Safe-Demon v1 based on YOLOv8; validated on 300 random frames, 98% detection accuracy (IoU>=0.5); 7-zone perspective partition of frame
semantic_segmentation: Yes (Fig. 3 per-pixel overlay); 19 classes (train...sky, Cityscapes-like set); model training data not reported
detection_tracking: YOLOv8 detection/segmentation of class at gaze and dominant class in gaze circle; no multi-object tracking
fixation_definition: Duration-based glance coding: <150 ms 'saccade', 150-700 ms 'fixation', >700 ms 'long fixation'; per-frame gaze = median of most compact DBSCAN cluster (eps=10 px, min_samples=2); spatial grouping criterion not reported
gaze_metrics: Proportions of glance types; semantic class at/around gaze; gaze quadrant; scene semantic composition; % class in gaze circle; no pupil, no blinks
kinematic_metrics: Instantaneous speed, accelerations (g), angular velocities (deg/s), 'smoothed' (method not reported); speed top SHAP feature for all targets
statistics: Descriptives (mean, SD, 95% CI, CV); per-participant Pearson chi-square + Bonferroni (Cramer's V); UNIANOVA User_ID x Section as FIXED effects (partial eta2); per-user k-NN vs NASA-TLX (70/30, pseudo-R2); per-user XGBoost/RF etc. with grid search + SHAP; ANOVA + Tukey on SHAP shares. No mixed models, no random effects
key_results: Glances: saccade 38.09%, fixation 36.43%, long fixation 25.47%; 3 gaze profiles; section effect significant but small (V 0.095-0.180); EEG User x Section interaction partial eta2 0.083 (Med) / 0.102 (Att); k-NN pseudo-R2 0.48-0.67; XGBoost glance accuracy 0.82-0.88; RF R2 0.82-0.94; visual/kinematic features drive gaze, OSM spatial features drive EEG indices; speed top feature everywhere
effect_sizes: Cramer's V 0.095-0.180; partial eta2 Meditation User 0.031, Section 0.002, UserxSection 0.083; Attention User 0.127, Section 0.016, UserxSection 0.102; ANOVA on SHAP shares F=84.22/13.76/67.70
limitations: Authors: small N, single path mostly separated/signalised, uncontrolled traffic, EEG contact/hair artefacts and dropouts, eye-tracker sunlight/connectivity losses, Hawthorne effect, recall bias, eSense interpretation underdetermined. Ours: pseudo-replication (frame rows as units), fixed participant effects, probable train/test leakage (interpolated 1 Hz EEG, multi-frame glances, split not reported), ordinal coding of nominal classes, Table 11 overall row inconsistent with rows, several citation errors, no pupil/HR
replicability_for_us: Gaze-semantic coding from scene video, OSM buffer features, segment NASA-TLX directly replicable with Aria; kinematics must be estimated from head-worn GPS/VIO (no vehicle sensors); EEG not available; replace their stats with GLMM/LMM and blocked CV
rq_informed: RQ1, RQ2, RQ3 (partially), RQ4 (inter-individual variability), workload question (NASA-TLX feasible; EEG fragile; no pupil/PPG evidence)
